value: Multiple regression analyses controlling for BMI, abstinence prior to scanning, gender and smoking status revealed a significant negative association between leptin plasma levels and alcohol cue-induced activation in the left and right caudate.

The negative association between leptin and cue-induced brain response might reflect a protective effect of leptin, such that it attenuates cue-reactivity, potentially reflecting a neural correlate of the reduced relapse risk.

value: Acylated ghrelin showed a significant positive association to alcohol cue-induced activation in several clusters of brain areas, including the bilateral insulae and parts of the superior and middle frontal gyri, as well as the middle cingulum, even after controlling for BMI, abstinence prior to scanning, gender and smoking status.
This is compatible with the hypothesis that increased plasma ghrelin levels sensitize reactions to alcohol cues by means of mesolimbic cue-reactivity and alcohol craving.
